channel.title: Xiaoyuan — Systems Writing
channel.description: Writing about distributed data systems, ML platforms, and AI agents.

item.title: Agent 41: Define the Business Outcome Before Deciding You Need an Agent
item.description: Move from “we want an Agent” back to task outcomes, current loss, responsibility boundaries, and completion evidence so a preferred solution becomes a verifiable business problem.

item.title: Agent 42: Requirements Research Must Reconstruct Real Work, Not Repeat the SOP
item.description: Use shadowing, artifact review, logs, and critical-incident reconstruction to find waiting, compensating actions, and implicit decision evidence outside the SOP.

item.title: Agent 46: Turn Requirements into a Verifiable Contract with a Task Contract
item.description: Connect business requirements, Tools, authorization, Human-in-the-Loop, Eval, and Pilot through inputs, capabilities, prohibited actions, completion evidence, and escalation conditions.

item.title: Agent 43: A Task Map Must Include State, Decisions, and Exceptions
item.description: Move beyond sequential flowcharts to a map of tasks, state, decisions, evidence, and exceptions so an Agent knows when to continue, clarify, or escalate.

item.title: Agent 45: Automatable Does Not Mean Worth Automating
item.description: Evaluate end-to-end benefit, human review, failure handling, Tool Coverage, verifiability, and risk cost together to estimate the real Automation Ceiling.

item.title: Agent 44: How to Choose Between a Workflow, Copilot, and Agent
item.description: Distinguish Workflow, Copilot, and Agent by path preplanning, dynamic evidence, action ownership, and result verification, then compose them instead of forcing one label.

item.title: LLM Infra 06: How Continuous Batching Changes Request Scheduling
item.description: Start from sequences of different lengths arriving continuously, then explain iteration-level scheduling, Token/KV budgets, fairness, chunked prefill, and preemption.

item.title: LLM Infra 03: How an Inference Benchmark Produces a Comparable Service Curve
item.description: Fix the workload distribution, arrival control, warm state, deployment manifest, and quality constraints to measure a service curve that capacity planning can consume.

item.title: LLM Infra 12: Coordinating Queuing, Rejection, and Scaling Across Time Scales
item.description: Put immediate admission, a bounded queue, slow provisioning, and scale-in draining into one capacity-control loop operating across multiple time scales.

item.title: LLM Infra 04: How to Derive Inference Capacity from Token Workload
item.description: Combine a workload envelope, per-Replica service curve, failure reserve, and provisioning lead time into a capacity range instead of guessing the Replica count from average GPU utilization.

item.title: LLM Infra 09: How the Bottleneck Determines the Inference Deployment Topology
item.description: Separate model fit, single-request latency, aggregate goodput, and Prefill/Decode resource asymmetry before choosing Replicas, Tensor/Pipeline Parallelism, Context Parallelism, or P/D disaggregation.

item.title: LLM Infra 05: Why a Runtime Can Reject Requests While GPU Memory Is Still Free
item.description: Separate the CUDA device, PyTorch allocator, and Runtime KV pool as three observation surfaces, then build an admission memory ledger for weights, KV Cache, temporary Activations, and workspace.

item.title: LLM Infra 16: How Tenant Identity Traverses the Inference Resource Chain
item.description: Carry trusted Tenant identity through the Queue, Model and Adapter, Prefix Cache, execution, logs, and usage evidence while separating logical isolation from hardware isolation.

item.title: LLM Infra 13: Which Execution Grains Must Inference Observability Align With
item.description: Align identity, timestamps, and outcomes across logical requests, attempts, executions, sequences, Replicas, and deployments so that aggregate metrics remain explainable.

item.title: LLM Infra 08: Why Quantization's Memory Savings Do Not Equal Deliverable Capacity
item.description: Separate Weight, Activation, and KV Cache quantization, then use a memory ledger, Kernel support, quality constraints, and a workload-specific service curve to determine whether quantization adds deliverable capacity.

item.title: LLM Infra 10: What State Must an Inference Scheduler Own?
item.description: Explain why cross-Replica scheduling cannot rely on queue length alone, and define the state boundaries among requests, Endpoint observations, placement decisions, affinity, and admission outcomes.

item.title: LLM Infra 02: Why Latency, Throughput, and Cost Cannot Be Optimized Separately
item.description: Separate TTFT, TPOT, end-to-end latency, throughput, goodput, and cost per Token, then turn performance goals into a service decision constrained by workload and quality.

item.title: LLM Infra 01: Start by Describing the Inference Workload
item.description: Build a workload envelope from input and output Tokens, Prefill/Decode, arrival shape, concurrency, and deadlines so that SLOs, Benchmarks, capacity planning, and scheduling consume the same model.

item.title: LLM Infra 15: How Model Upgrades, Rollouts, and Fallbacks Preserve the Deployment Contract
item.description: Bind the Model, Tokenizer, Template, Adapter, Engine image, Runtime configuration, and capability claims into a release manifest, then use the same workload to drive canary evaluation and rollback decisions.

item.title: LLM Infra 11: Preventing Cold-Start Amplification in Multi-Model and Adapter Routing
item.description: When the number of models and Adapters exceeds resident capacity, separate artifact identity from residency observation, then manage cold starts through load reservations, popularity, and routing stability.

item.title: LLM Infra 07: Why Prefix Cache Reuse Cannot Rely on Matching Text Alone
item.description: Separate Prefix/KV Cache reuse into deployment namespace, Token block identity, and isolation policy so identical text is not mistaken for compatible state.

item.title: LLM Infra 14: When Can a Failed Streaming Inference Request Be Retried?
item.description: Separate logical requests, attempts, executions, partial delivery, and cancellation to define the boundaries of retry, restart, and explicit failure for streaming inference.

item.title: Agent 23: Artifact References, Retention, and Deletion Must Be Separate Layers
item.description: Separate Message references, existing download capabilities, logical Artifact deletion, lineage retention, and provider deletion of a scoped object-version target set.

item.title: Agent 05: Long-Conversation Compression Must Preserve Rebuildable Source Boundaries
item.description: Use coverage, dependency closure, revisions, and a safe recent window so conversation summaries can be invalidated and rebuilt after corrections.

item.title: Agent 31: How Durable Job Cancellation, Results, and Delivery Converge
item.description: Use claim leases, generation fencing, an intermediate cancelling state, and conditional delivery to handle duplicate workers, late results, and user cancellation.

item.title: Agent 10: Execution Journals and Checkpoints Must Recover Together
item.description: Recover Agent state without repeating unknown effects by combining an authoritative Journal, idempotent projections, and cursor-bound Checkpoints.

item.title: Agent 03: Hook Composition Order Must Be an Execution Contract
item.description: Define Hook phases, mutation rights, short-circuiting, cleanup, failure, and replay from a disabled Tool that reappears in a request.

item.title: Agent 29: A Verifiable Confirmation Protocol for High-Risk Actions
item.description: Bind user confirmation to a specific action, parameters, resource revision, identity, and expiry so stale approval cannot be reused.

item.title: Agent 22: Why One File Needs Both an Artifact Identity and a Workspace Reference
item.description: Model a file's cross-stage lifecycle with Artifact identity, Workspace references, and structured mutation preconditions.

item.title: Agent 08: Which Capabilities Should an Agent Expose on Each Turn?
item.description: Separate instruction resources, the Tool surface, Connectors, and MCP to decide which capabilities the model actually sees on one Turn.

item.title: Agent 09: Ordering, Consistency, and Cancellation for Concurrent Tools
item.description: Separate event announcement, handler invocation, completion order, Context order, shared mutation, and layered cancellation guarantees.

item.title: Agent 21: How Connectors, MCP, and the Host Control Plane Divide Responsibility
item.description: Separate the Connector credential boundary, the MCP protocol, and the host control plane to identify who owns capability discovery, versioning, health, and authorization.

item.title: Agent 38: Context Assembly Evaluation Cannot Stop at Recall
item.description: Evaluate a Context projection with required information, citations, pollution, conflict handling, and budget efficiency.

item.title: Agent 04: Context Is a Constrained Projection
item.description: Resolve provenance, authorization, conflicts, and budget decisions before provider shaping so that every model input remains explainable and can degrade safely.

item.title: Agent 16: Who Should Own the Execution State of Delegated Work?
item.description: Choose a parent Run, Child Run, Job, or Workflow according to completion ownership, lifecycle, durability, cancellation, and result consumption.

item.title: Agent 32: Recovering Durable Jobs Across Queues and Workflows
item.description: Separate Queue redelivery, event publication, and partial success across state owners, then choose the right recovery mechanism for each failure boundary.

item.title: Agent 36: Which Layer of the Result Should a Grader Verify?
item.description: Place deterministic assertions, rule-based Graders, LLM Judges, and domain results for Tools and Context in one evidence hierarchy.

item.title: Agent 34: Making Nondeterministic Evaluations Comparable
item.description: Use case × configuration × trial, dataset tiers, and a complete manifest to make Agent evaluations reproducible and comparable.

item.title: Agent 15: The Owner of a Failure State Chooses the Recovery Action
item.description: Choose retry, fallback, repair, reconciliation, or replanning according to whether the Model, Tool, Plan, or Service owns the failure.

item.title: Agent 20: Identity and Authorization Must Survive the Execution Chain
item.description: Separate subject, actor, execution identity, credential, and authorization so authority can cross Queues, Tools, and Child Runs.

item.title: Agent 01: The Agent's Minimal Core: Loop, Turn, and Execution State
item.description: Starting from a Tool write with an unknown outcome, this article uses a minimal state model to separate the Agent Loop, Model Turn, Tool Execution, and Attempt.

item.title: Agent 17: Memory Writes, Versions, and the Current View
item.description: Connect write gates, Writer trust domains, version chains, and the current view into a complete lifecycle for long-term Memory.

item.title: Agent 18: How Retrieved Memory Enters Context
item.description: Connect candidate generation, current-view filtering, reranking, authorization, and the Context budget into one read decision.

item.title: Agent 19: How to Test Memory's Persistent-Risk Defenses
item.description: Treat Memory defenses as the system under test, using attack traces, rejected writes, corrections, expiry, and cross-tenant cases to measure restraint, freshness, and leakage.

item.title: Agent 06: Why Model Fallback Needs Both a Router and an Adapter
item.description: Separate model selection from provider protocol shaping so that fallback does not change Tool, message, or streaming-event semantics.

item.title: Agent 27: Tenant-Private Objects Must Carry Their Isolation Domain
item.description: Propagate tenant identity into Queues, caches, Artifacts, Traces, Credentials, and background execution to prevent derived objects from leaking across tenants.

item.title: Agent 33: A Shared Semantic Model for Agent Logs, Metrics, and Traces
item.description: Fix the grain, logical IDs, Attempts, and outcome taxonomy before connecting Agent logs, metrics, traces, and cost facts.

item.title: Agent 40: Platform Boundaries Follow State Ownership and Reversal Conditions
item.description: Decide whether an Agent capability should become a platform service using Sources of Truth, failure domains, resource curves, adoption cost, and reversal conditions.

item.title: Agent 39: Closing the Loop Between Evaluation and Production
item.description: Share the production execution path with Eval, then use Shadow, Canary, and evidence-backed bad-case ingestion to build a reversible release loop.

item.title: Agent 12: Why Real-Time Output Is Not an Execution Record
item.description: Separate durable execution events, lossy transport signals, and client cursors so that reconnection does not rewrite execution facts.

item.title: Agent 30: How Budgets, Quotas, and Backpressure Work Together
item.description: Separate per-Run budgets, subject quotas, burst limits, and hotspot backpressure, then propagate admission decisions through the execution chain.

item.title: Agent 14: How to Revise a Plan Safely When Its Assumptions Change
item.description: Model a Plan as a revisable Artifact with revisions, dependencies, assumptions, and evidence lineage—not as an execution state machine.

item.title: Agent 02: How Run Configuration Stabilizes for Each Turn
item.description: Separate long-lived policy from per-turn snapshots, and constrain how control Hooks and read-only Observers may affect those snapshots.

item.title: Agent 13: How New Input Enters the Next Turn During Execution
item.description: Separate steering, follow-up, cancellation, and durable admission to define when new input is accepted and consumed during a Run.

item.title: Agent 24: Sandbox Lifecycle and the Control Plane

item.title: Agent 28: Which Runtime Threats a Sandbox Must Constrain
item.description: Define the Sandbox Runtime threat boundary across command, filesystem, network egress, secret, and resource controls.

item.title: Agent 11: How a Session Tree Supports Recovery
item.description: Separate branched Session history, Context projection, and the execution Journal, then show how the host restores configuration and settled results from a Checkpoint.

item.title: Agent 07: A Tool Is an Execution Contract for the Model
item.description: Build a complete Tool contract from model-facing Schema through trusted execution, external side effects, normalized results, and repairable errors.

item.title: Agent 37: Which Failure Layer Should a Tool System Eval Diagnose?
item.description: Evaluate Tool selection, arguments, repair, mutation precision, and Task success separately so a final answer cannot hide execution errors.

item.title: Agent 35: Turning Production Traces into Verifiable Evidence
item.description: Convert sanitized production Traces into reproducible regression cases while preserving the boundary of assertion-time evidence.

item.title: Agent 26: How to Stop External Content from Producing a Tool Effect

item.title: Agent 25: How a Workspace Recovers Across Runtimes
item.description: Use Workspace identity, Runtime profile compatibility, and leases to decide whether a stateful execution environment should be reused, migrated, or quarantined.
